text: I stood beside the chain-link fence at Tamsin Reservoir on Tuesday morning as crews finished the long-delayed repair, and project foreman Leena Voss told me the total cost came to 12 million. She said the work, which began after last winter’s partial wall collapse, included reinforcing the spillway, replacing cracked intake pipes, and clearing silt from the eastern basin. “It was expensive, but we needed it done right,” Voss said, while a pair of operators tested the new valves. County engineer Martin Pell confirmed the figure to me by phone later in the day, adding that the reservoir should be back at full capacity by early March.
